title: Part-time or full-time private chef: how many hours?
body_html:
The part-time or full-time question for a private chef is really a question about weekly hours. Count the meals you want a chef to cover each week and the hours behind them; that number, not budget first, decides which arrangement fits. The full-time private chef service in Dubai page sets out the recurring arrangements, and this guide shows how to read your own week honestly.

What the weekly hours decide

Your weekHours it really takesArrangement that fits
Two or three family dinnersA few hours per visitPart-time visits on fixed days
Daily lunches or dinnersMost afternoons, every dayA full-time arrangement
Diet-plan cooking for oneBatch blocks, not daily presencePart-time with a weekly block
Large household plus staff mealsFull days, early to lateFull-time

A decision checklist

  • Count the meals, not the days: three dinners and five lunches are different weeks.
  • Decide who shops, and where ingredients come from, before comparing rates.
  • Check your kitchen's real capacity: one cooktop shapes the schedule.
  • List dietary requirements in writing — halal-first is standard.
  • Confirm whether children's or staff meals fall inside the same arrangement.
  • Ask about cover for the chef's days off before, not after, you commit.

Scaling up over time (hypothetical)

A couple starts with two part-time afternoons a week covering dinners and a batch-prep block. A new baby adds lunches; a move to a villa adds staff meals for two helpers. Each step adds hours, and the arrangement is reviewed before it is extended — the cheaper mistake is staying part-time on paper while quietly asking for full-time presence.

Next step: send your weekly meal count, household size and any dietary notes through the full-time chef page and the right arrangement is proposed with a schedule. Related reading: planning cover for a chef's day off and booking a private chef on a monthly basis.
